title: Route-level A/B testing: finalize PRD, beta/GA gating, and launch readiness criteria
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Why this ticket exists
We have a working PRD draft + early implementation work underway for route-level A/B testing in Console. Before we enable beta (and later GA), we need a single, explicit set of requirements + gating criteria that align Product, SRE, Security/Compliance, and the teams shipping the backend + telemetry.

This ticket is the PM “source of truth” for:
- Final PRD scope for v1 (beta) and GA
- Beta/GA gating by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Internal launch readiness checklist (SRE guardrails, audit logging, permissions, runbooks, docs)
- Clear success metrics (adoption + reliability)

- Design spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-route-ab-testing-workflows.json

## In scope (v1 beta)
### Customer value
- Define an experiment at the API route level (per project) to split production traffic across 2 variants (A/B) with deterministic assignment.
- Measure variant outcomes using standardized metrics (latency, TTFT, token counts, cost attribution, error/timeout rates).
- View results in Console: side-by-side comparisons and guardrail status.

### Functional requirements to call “beta-ready”
1) Experiment lifecycle in Console
- Create experiment (route + eligibility + traffic split + variants)
- Validate config (pre-flight checks)
- Start/Stop
- Rollback workflow (explicit revert to control, plus audit event)
- Clear messaging for overlapping rollouts/route ownership

2) Deterministic assignment
- Stable across retries/stream reconnects per ADR-0187
- Documented assignment semantics (what inputs are used; how stickiness works)

3) Measurement hooks + exposure logging
- Exposure event emitted at gateway with schema v1
- Low overhead with sampling controls
- Required metrics: p50/p95/p99 E2E latency, TTFT, tokens in/out, per-request cost attribution, error/timeout rates
- Guard against high-cardinality tags (enforce allowlist)

4) Guardrails and safe ops
- SRE-defined thresholds for auto-alert and (where supported) auto-rollback hook
- Audit log events for experiment create/update/start/stop/rollback
- A documented emergency disable path (kill switch) and runbook

5) Documentation + internal enablement
- Public docs draft ready before beta enablement (even if gated)
- Internal support playbook (what to check when metrics look “wrong”, how to validate assignment)

## Out of scope (v1 beta)
- Multi-armed bandits / automated optimization
- Arbitrary customer-defined metrics ingestion
- Client-side SDK experimentation helpers beyond docs/examples
- Online judge sampling pipeline as a requirement for beta (we can run it as an internal/professional-services motion)

## Tier gating proposal (decision needed)
### Beta
- Hosted: enabled for selected design partners behind feature flag
- Dedicated: enabled for selected design partners behind feature flag (requires capacity-aware safeguards; see GA criteria)
- Private: not enabled in beta by default (requires additional controls for customer-managed telemetry + retention policies)

### GA
- Hosted: GA once guardrails + dashboards are stable and we meet success + reliability metrics
- Dedicated: GA requires additional “capacity-aware” warnings and an explicit ‘max traffic %’ constraint to avoid regional 429s (see incident follow-up)
- Private: follow-on milestone; GA in Private requires security review for log retention/access, and “customer-managed export” story

## GA criteria (proposed)
### Reliability / safety
- No Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents attributable to experiment routing/telemetry for 30 days post-beta expansion
- Guardrail alerting coverage validated in all enabled regions
- Emergency disable validated in staging + 1 prod dry-run (no customer impact)
- Audit events validated end-to-end (Console action -> audit event -> export/SIEM where applicable)

### Measurement integrity
- Exposure logging sampling documented + default sampling rate chosen; back-of-envelope cost and storage reviewed by Telemetry
- Metric parity checks: Console experiment dashboard within agreed tolerance of baseline latency dashboard (define acceptable deltas due to sampling/aggregation)

### UX readiness
- Create/validate/start flow passes design review and internal dogfood feedback addressed (warnings, copy clarity, control semantics)
- Results dashboard includes: exposure counts, variant comparison for core metrics, and confidence indicator copy that discourages over-interpretation at low sample sizes

### Adoption / value signal
- At least 3 beta partners successfully run an experiment for >= 7 days and can answer one of:
  - reduced cost at same latency
  - improved latency at same cost
  - improved quality (offline eval) without unacceptable latency regression
- Support load: < 3 P1 support cases per 10 active experiments related to confusion/incorrect setup

## Internal launch checklist (must be explicit)
SRE (Owner: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant)
- [ ] Guardrail thresholds agreed and codified (latency + error-rate)
- [ ] Alert routing verified (on-call ownership)
- [ ] Runbook published and linked from Console (internal)
- [ ] Kill switch / emergency disable verified

Security/Compliance (Owner: Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman)
- [ ] RBAC review: who can create/start/stop/rollback experiments
- [ ] Audit event coverage validated against spec
- [ ] Privacy review: exposure logging fields and retention meet ADR-0188

Telemetry/Analytics (Owner: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman)
- [ ] Exposure event schema version locked (v1)
- [ ] Cardinality review complete; allowlist enforcement in place
- [ ] Cost attribution by experiment/variant validated
- [ ] Aggregation job SLAs understood (data freshness for dashboard)

Docs/Enablement (Owner: Elliot Price / Wei Chen)
- [ ] Public docs PR ready (gated messaging ok)
- [ ] Internal troubleshooting guide for Support/Solutions

## Open questions / decisions needed this week
1) What are the default assignment inputs (and what is the documented customer override story, if any)?
2) Do we require auto-rollback for beta, or is alert-only sufficient (with runbook)?
3) Dedicated tier constraint: do we enforce a max traffic % per variant by default to reduce capacity incidents, or only warn?
4) Console terminology: “Control” vs “Variant A” naming defaults (Support feedback indicates confusion)

## Acceptance criteria
- PRD v1 finalized (Confluence) with explicit beta scope and GA criteria (linked here)
- Beta gating decision recorded: Hosted + Dedicated flag behavior + Private stance
- Launch checklist agreed by SRE + Security with named owners and “must-have” items
- Release readiness definition posted in #eng-releases thread and linked to ENG-2848 rollout plan

comments: 2026-02-06 (Paula Mendes): Added minimum telemetry requirements to beta gating section. Strongly recommend we do not enable beta UI until exposure events are emitted from gateway in at least one region + validated in the reporting dataset; otherwise support burden will be high.

2026-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): For beta enablement we need (1) documented guardrail thresholds, (2) at least alerting wired to on-call, and (3) a tested kill-switch path. Auto-rollback can be “soft required” for GA but not strictly required for the first two design partners.

2026-02-12 (Marcus Lin): Security review focus areas: RBAC for experiment lifecycle actions and audit log completeness. Also confirm no raw user identifiers in exposure events; hashed IDs must be irreversibly derived per ADR-0188.

2026-02-18 (Tessa Morgan): Create/start flow needs explicit warning if experiment overlaps with an active canary/rollout for same route. Also recommend copy change: avoid calling it “control” by default; show ‘Baseline (A)’ and ‘Candidate (B)’ with editable labels.

2026-02-21 (Dylan Brooks): Engineering is aligned with the gating plan. One risk: Dedicated tier needs capacity-aware validation (prevent 90/10 split that still overloads variant pool in a region). Suggest we add a pre-flight warning based on recent headroom metrics; can be non-blocking for beta but should be GA requirement.
